description: Single-panel engineering stress-strain plot (property_mechanical) recorded at room temperature for a Fe-0.25C-3Mn-2Al-0.4Si medium-Mn low-density steel after cold rolling and annealing. The x-axis is "Engineering Strain/%" (0-35, ticks every 5) and the y-axis is "Engineering Stress/MPa" (0-1400, ticks every 200). A boxed legend at the top right identifies three curves by annealing temperature: 750°C (black), 800°C (red) and 850°C (blue); the text "Air cooling" is printed inside the plot at lower right. The blue 850°C curve rises most steeply to the highest peak, lying between the 1200 and 1400 MPa gridlines and close to 1300 MPa, then softens and terminates just below 10% strain. The red 800°C curve peaks just above the 1200 MPa gridline at roughly 5% strain and ends near 13% strain at about the 1000-1200 MPa level. The black 750°C curve yields more gradually into a long plateau slightly above the 1000 MPa gridline that persists from roughly 13% to 30% strain before a gentle fall, ending near 33% strain. The figure therefore demonstrates a strength-ductility trade-off: raising the annealing temperature from 750°C to 850°C raises peak stress but sharply reduces elongation.

subfigures.description: Engineering stress-strain curves of three annealed conditions plotted on one pair of axes (x: Engineering Strain/% 0-35; y: Engineering Stress/MPa 0-1400). Legend: 750°C (black), 800°C (red), 850°C (blue); annotation 'Air cooling' in the lower-right plot area. No error bars or replicate curves are shown.

observations.observation: The plot contains exactly three engineering stress-strain curves, colour-coded in the legend as 750°C (black), 800°C (red) and 850°C (blue).
The axes are labelled 'Engineering Stress/MPa' (y, 0 to 1400, ticks every 200) and 'Engineering Strain/%' (x, 0 to 35, ticks every 5).
The annotation 'Air cooling' is printed inside the plot at the lower right, indicating the post-annealing cooling condition of the tested specimens.
The 850°C (blue) curve reaches the highest peak stress of the three, with the maximum lying between the 1200 and 1400 MPa gridlines rather than on a printed value.
The 850°C (blue) curve terminates at the smallest strain of the three, just below the 10% strain mark.
The 800°C (red) curve peaks just above the 1200 MPa gridline at approximately 5% strain and ends near 13% strain.
The 750°C (black) curve shows a gradual yield and a long flat plateau slightly above the 1000 MPa gridline, extending from about 13% to about 30% strain before a gentle decline to roughly 33% strain.
The figure shows a trade-off: increasing the annealing temperature from 750°C to 850°C increases the peak stress but greatly reduces the elongation to fracture.
No numeric stress or strain values are printed on any curve, and no error bars or replicate curves are displayed despite three samples being tested per condition.
The caption states that the panel presents engineering stress-strain curves at different annealing temperatures.
The citing text states the experimental steel composition is Fe-0.25C-3Mn-2Al-0.4Si (mass fraction) melted in a vacuum induction furnace.

The citing text states the cold-rolled specimens were annealed at 750°C, 800°C and 850°C for 30 min, air-cooled, then held at 400°C for 30 min and air-cooled, giving specimens designated ANT750, ANT800 and ANT850.
The citing text states tensile tests used an Instron 3382 machine with 15 mm × 5.0 mm × 1.0 mm gauge specimens at a strain rate of 5 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹, with three samples per group for repeatability.
The citing text frames this figure as validation of a YS prediction model built from strengthening-mechanism contributions and literature data.

unreadable_items: No panel is illegible; the exact peak stress and elongation values cannot be read because no numeric data labels are printed on the curves (values are only bracketed by the 200 MPa and 5% gridlines).
